predecessors.note: 'The KMT troops and their dependents began crossing into Burma in late December 1949 and early January 1950' after the PLA entered Yunnan; the territory is Burma's Kengtung State.

successors.note: Between 31 March and 17 April 1961 Taiwan evacuated about 4,400 guerrillas and dependents; an estimated 450-700 remained in Burma or fled to Thailand and Laos, where the remnants dominated the Golden Triangle opium trade until the 1980s.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. By March 1950 about 1,500 men held ground 'between Kengtung City and Tachilek'; Burmese forces took Tachilek within weeks of the June 1950 ultimatum (ledger, 1950-07). A 50 km circle is the researcher's reading; the keyframe covers 1949 only because the July 1950 loss and gain are events and the 1950 keyframe shows the state after them.

correction.text: Mong Hsat, 'centrally located in a fertile basin' in Kengtung State, the KMT base from July 1950: a 60 km circle cut to Shan State

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (replaces the former 1951-1960 keyframe's first years). From July 1950 the KMT's base is Mong Hsat, 'centrally located in a fertile basin' in Kengtung State; the page says 'The Burmese Army made several attempts over the next two years but were unsuccessful in ousting the KMT from Mong Hsat'. The 60 km circle is the researcher's reading; the page gives no area. Tachilek is lost in July 1950 (an event).

correction.text: the KMT's Shan territory 'between the Salween River on the west, the China border on the east, and Thailand on the south': the researcher's reading as a 100 km circle at Mong Hsat plus a 60 km circle at Tachileik, cut to Shan State; the page gives no area

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the failed attempt to re-enter China in August 1952 'The KMT stopped concentrating their forces near the China border in late 1952' and spread over the Shan states; 'Eventually it gained control over the Shan territories between the Salween River on the west, the China border on the east, and Thailand on the south'. The page gives no area; the 100 km Mong Hsat circle and 60 km Tachileik circle are the researcher's reading. Strength rose from over 4,000 (April 1951) to 6,000 (end of 1951) and doubled in 1952. The 1953-54 evacuation (three phases, 7 November 1953 to 7 May 1954; Li Mi announced the dissolution of the army on 30 May 1954, infobox 'Disbanded 30 May 1954 (officially)') left 'about 6,000 irregular KMT troops' in Burma and changed no border, so no event or keyframe is drawn for it. The shape holds to the April 1961 evacuation: the page names no place taken in the 1960-61 operations, so no earlier shrinking is drawn.

ledger.note: 1950-07: the Burmese army contests the KMT's Mong Hsat base. Burmese forces captured Tachilek 'within weeks' of the June 1950 demand to surrender or leave, and 'The Burmese Army made several attempts over the next two years but were unsuccessful in ousting the KMT from Mong Hsat'; the zone widens to the whole KMT country in late 1952 (see the war's zone and the 1961 contest_end). Burma appealed to the UN in March 1953 and a Four-Nation Military Commission sat in Bangkok on 22 May 1953. The year is the page's; the 60 km circle is the researcher's reading.

The year is the page's (no month); the extent is the researcher's reading, so confidence 2. This replaces the earlier dating to 1951, which the page does not support.

wars.outcome: Burma took Tachilek in 1950 and failed for two years to oust the KMT from Mong Hsat; the KMT spread over the Shan states in late 1952; Burma appealed to the UN in March 1953; the 1953-1954 evacuations to Taiwan left about 6,000 irregulars; joint Burmese-PLA operations in 1960-1961 'broke the back' of the irregulars and Taiwan evacuated about 4,400 more in April 1961.

certainty.note: An irregular army's zone with no recorded boundary; only Tachilek and Mong Hsat are named places.

notes: Rebel (foreign irregular) state added by se-04-x; the union-of-burma dossier (se-01-j) lists the Kuomintang army as a counterpart needing a dossier. The page gives no area and no map: Tachileik and Mong Hsat circles and the 'Salween to China to Thailand' core are the researcher's readings; the late-1952 extent is confidence 2. Not on the page: Duan Xiwen, Li Mi's movements before 1953, Operation Mekong, Mae Salong; the Chinese 'Operation Mekong' and 'Naga Naing' names are not used. The KMT's remnants in Thailand after 1961 (Santikhiri, Golden Triangle) are outside the dossier. The 1953-54 evacuations (7 November 1953 to 7 May 1954) left about 6,000 irregulars and changed no border. Counterpart people-s-republic-of-china in the war entry is the PLA of the 1960-1961 joint operation. Page budget: 3 pages. Repair pass 2026-10-25 (page re-read): (1) the spread over the Shan country is 1952, not 1951: 'The KMT stopped concentrating their forces near the China border in late 1952' after the failed re-entry of August 1952; the gain is dated 1952 (no month) at confidence 2 and the gain region subtracts the Mong Hsat circle already held. (2) Keyframes are now 1949 (Tachileik), 1950-1951 (Mong Hsat circle) and 1952-1961 (the Shan territory); the former 1961 Tachileik-only keyframe is dropped because the page names no place taken in 1960-61, so the 1961 loss and dissolve take the shape the keyframe holds. (3) The contest_start is dated 1950-07, not 1952 as the reviewer suggested: the page has Burma taking Tachilek 'within weeks' of June 1950 and failing for two years to oust the KMT from Mong Hsat, which is fighting that holds ground; the zone is the Mong Hsat circle until the late-1952 spread, and the war entry already began in 1950. (4) The capitals end at Mong Hsat; Chiang Rai (infobox, 1961) is in Thailand outside every shape and is not drawn. (5) The 1953-54 evacuation and Li Mi's 30 May 1954 dissolution announcement changed no border and have no event type; they are in the 1952-1961 keyframe note. The Kengtung coordinates were not looked up (Tachileik still stands in for the 1949-50 headquarters).
